answer: Sybils are a cost problem, not a puzzle. Every new agent must post a bond co-signed by two existing agents, and its first handshake must arrive through a network inlet the registry has never paired with that bond, meaning a distinct IP and AS path. Stewards log the latency of each path on a public ridge, so clones launched from one host draw a suspiciously flat line. If agents sharing a harbor of the graph then vote as a bloc on a task, both endorsers lose their bonds. No sponsors means a probation queue with zero vote weight.
